newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly lower in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly lower in volatile trade.

text.p: Swiss shares ended a volatile session on Thursday slightly lower in a correction of Wednesday's three percent jump.
Trade was described as nervous and many stocks were seen leaping up and down, also partially due to derivatives-related transactions, dealers said.
Opening losses on Wall Street put some pressure on prices.
"I think the market will stay volatile and we will see a sideways movement," one dealer said, citing the lack of important economic data in the next few sessions.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell 20.7 points 0.35 percent to 5,849.24.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 0.51 points at 3,709.09.
Bourse volume did not reach Wednesday's level, but still stood at a solid 2.85 billion Swiss francs.
One trader said the dollar's strong rise did not seem to affect prices much.

Novartis, which announced a 19 percent rise in first half sales to 16.6 billion Swiss francs, ended 46 francs down at 2,400. Dealers said sales figures were mostly in line with expectations, but some investors took profits following the stock's recent rise.
Roche was reportedly lifted by switches from Novartis, adding 235 francs to 14,750.
Specialty chemicals firm Clariant, which on Wednesday reported better-than-expected sales for the first six months, gained 28 francs to 1,078.
Financials were mixed. While CS Group lost two francs to 202.75, SBC advanced 2.50 francs to 423.50.
Shares of Swiss Life continued their recent strong rise, jumping 72 francs or 10 percent to 800.
Most traders said the stock was clearly overvalued.
A Swiss Life spokesman explained the rise with the fact that the free float of the shares was low and demand was high. "There have been certain exaggerations," the spokesman added.
However, the liquidity should substantially increase over the next weeks due to the conversion of a convertible issue, he said.
